newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Countrywide sees inevitable NZ mortgage rate rises.
newsitem.headline: Countrywide sees inevitable NZ mortgage rate rises.

text.p: Countrywide Bank managing director David Wolfenden said on Friday it was inevitable mortgage interest rates would rise after a big surge in 90 day bill rates.
"I believe all banks will have to move it is inevitable. we cannot sustain that level of wholesale rate," Wolfenden said in a telephone interview.
Ninety day bank bills were at 8.45 percent at the time of the interview compared with a 7.70 percent close on Thursday.
He said the bank needed to do its own analysis before making a decision.
"Unless there is a dramatic shift next week it is inevitable we will have to adjust our rates," he said.
"If the current bill rate remains at around the 8.50 mark you are talking in excess of 10 percent -- mid tens," Wolfenden said.
He said the bank would have to look at all its mortgage rates as part of the review.
Countrywide offers a floating rate mortgage of 8.95 percent.
"It (the rate at 8.95 percent) doesn't make a lot of sense does it?" he said.
